section_summary: This section examines Japan’s wartime budget, bond issues, foreign trade, gold reserves, and access to foreign credit in 1939. It includes a lengthy Reuters analysis, embassy and military reports, State Department memoranda, and a claim concerning missing Japanese government bonds. File notes point to related records on sanctions, credit, and naval spending.

subfiles.title: Bonds and Currency
subfiles.about: Reviews Japanese bond issues and currency circulation.
subfiles.summary: Bond absorption and the post-year-end contraction in note circulation are presented as signs that inflation remains controlled.

subfiles.title: Analysis of Financial Situation in Japan
subfiles.from: Willys R. Peck, U.S. Embassy, Chungking
subfiles.about: Transmits Reuters’ complete analysis of Japanese finances.
subfiles.summary: Peck forwards the X-Ray Economic Service analysis, following earlier telegrams summarizing it and Arthur N. Young’s comments.

subfiles.title: What Is Japan’s Financial Position?
subfiles.about: Assesses Japan’s ability to withstand economic retaliation.
subfiles.summary: The analysis separates trade within the yen bloc from trade that earns foreign exchange and estimates substantial balance-of-payments deficits in 1936–1938. It describes reduced shipping and tourism income, gold sales, tighter payment terms, and dwindling raw-material stocks. It concludes that continued deficits could exhaust Japan’s gold reserves and increase its vulnerability to Western economic measures.

subfiles.title: Corrections to despatch No. 125 enclosure
subfiles.about: Corrects wording and a Manchukuo trade figure in the Reuters enclosure.
subfiles.summary: Peck supplies two corrections to the financial analysis transmitted with despatch No. 125.

subfiles.title: Chinese Finance Ministry statement on public finance
subfiles.about: Points to a despatch enclosing a China Press clipping.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to a Chinese Finance Ministry statement on public finance in China and Japan.

subfiles.title: British financial credits to Japan
subfiles.about: Points to information on reducing British short-term credits to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to British government activity concerning short-term credit facilities for Japan.

subfiles.title: Proposed sale of locomotives to Japanese interests
subfiles.from: Green, State Department Division of Controls
subfiles.about: Points to a conversation about a locomotive sale.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to a conversation with Frank C. Wright on a proposed Lehigh Valley Railroad sale.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference to 894.50/109
subfiles.about: Directs the reader to another decimal-file entry.
subfiles.summary: Handwritten cross-reference, apparently to file 894.50/109.

subfiles.title: Japan’s economic vulnerability
subfiles.about: Points to a despatch on possible economic sanctions.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to articles, clippings, and Japanese foreign-trade returns concerning sanctions.

subfiles.title: National City Bank policy in the Far East
subfiles.from: Adams, State Department Far Eastern Division
subfiles.about: Points to a bank-policy conversation.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to discussion of financial facilities involving bank vice president Hart, Hamilton, and Adams.

subfiles.title: Credits for exports from the United States to Japan
subfiles.about: Points to a conversation with A. H. De Friest.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to Japanese business interest in obtaining U.S. export credits.

subfiles.title: Japanese naval replenishment program
subfiles.about: Points to figures on planned naval spending.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to a telegram on warship construction and other naval supplies.

subfiles.title: Gold Released from Hoarding
subfiles.about: Reports gold disclosed under Japan’s gold-hoarding law.
subfiles.summary: Creswell reports that declarations had brought about ¥100 million in gold to light by January 1939, including about ¥35 million from Formosa.

subfiles.title: Possibility of extending credits to Japan
subfiles.from: Hamilton, State Department Far Eastern Division
subfiles.about: Points to a memorandum on engineering work in Japanese-controlled China.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference concerning possible credits linked to J. G. White Engineering Corporation construction work.

subfiles.title: Appropriations for 1939–1940 Budget
subfiles.about: Summarizes Japanese budget appropriations and authorized bond issues.
subfiles.summary: Creswell reports enacted and pending appropriations, transfers between accounts, and ¥5.65 billion in authorized bond issues. He cautions that unfinished legislation and complex transfers prevent a definitive budget total.

subfiles.title: Treasury transmission of press-conference excerpt
subfiles.about: Sends an excerpt about possible Japanese borrowing.
subfiles.summary: Glasser supplies the requested excerpt from the Treasury Secretary’s December 19, 1938 press conference.

subfiles.title: Secretary Morgenthau on Japanese loans
subfiles.about: Addresses whether Japan could seek a U.S. loan or credit.
subfiles.summary: Morgenthau says Japan could apply to the Export-Import Bank, subject to applicable lending restrictions.

subfiles.title: 1938 Financial Annual of Japan
subfiles.about: Transmits copies of Japan’s 1938 financial and economic annual.
subfiles.summary: Grew forwards three English-language copies of the Japanese Finance Department’s annual.

subfiles.title: Siegelstein letter concerning Hovey estate bonds
subfiles.about: Announces a formal claim over missing Japanese bonds.
subfiles.summary: Siegelstein says the estate will file a sworn claim against Japan and pursue discovery against the Yokohama Specie Bank.

subfiles.title: Hackworth reply to Siegelstein
subfiles.about: Acknowledges the planned claim and supplies an earlier reply.
subfiles.summary: Hackworth states that the Department answered Siegelstein’s December letter and encloses a copy for consideration before filing a claim.

subfiles.title: Proposed Swiss loan to Japan
subfiles.about: Reviews Japan’s renewed approach to the Swiss National Bank.
subfiles.summary: The division recommends no action, noting Swiss resistance to the proposed loan.

subfiles.title: Japanese approach to Swiss National Bank
subfiles.about: Reports a renewed Japanese request for a large Swiss loan.
subfiles.summary: Harrison says Swiss officials reacted unfavorably to a purportedly nonmilitary loan proposal backed by exporters.

subfiles.title: Paraphrase of Bern telegram No. 44
subfiles.about: Restates the report on a proposed Swiss loan to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Paraphrase records the Japanese approach and unfavorable Swiss reaction.

subfiles.title: Transmission of Bern and Paris telegrams
subfiles.about: Forwards copies of two diplomatic telegrams.
subfiles.summary: Six copies each of telegrams from Bern and Paris are enclosed.

subfiles.title: Siegelstein submission of Hovey claim
subfiles.about: Submits the Hovey estate petition and supporting affidavit.
subfiles.summary: Siegelstein acknowledges Hackworth’s reply and lodges Cohen’s petition and Sindelar’s affidavit with the Department.

subfiles.title: Petition of H. Bernard Cohen against the Imperial Japanese Government
subfiles.about: Seeks diplomatic assistance in recovering payment for missing Japanese government bonds.
subfiles.summary: Cohen describes the Hovey estate’s roughly $14,000 in Japanese 1905 sterling bonds, missing since Hovey’s death, and efforts to replace them. He alleges that the Yokohama Specie Bank insisted on indemnity from one surety company, which refused to issue it despite alternatives offered by the estate. The petition asks the State Department to present a claim to Japan and obtain replacement and redemption of the bonds.

subfiles.title: Affidavit of William A. Sindelar
subfiles.about: Supports the Hovey estate’s claim for missing Japanese bonds.
subfiles.summary: Sindelar recounts the estate’s probate history, investigation of the missing bonds, and successful replacement of French bonds through an indemnity arrangement. He describes unsuccessful negotiations with the Yokohama Specie Bank and American Surety Company, lists the Japanese bonds and serial numbers, and joins Cohen’s request for relief.

subfiles.title: State Department reply on Hovey bond claim
subfiles.about: Declines to present the Hovey estate claim diplomatically at this stage.
subfiles.summary: Hackworth says the petition and affidavit offer no evidence or legal argument establishing a right to replacement bonds or acceptance of the offered indemnity. He indicates that any legal right should be established through appropriate New York judicial proceedings.

subfiles.title: Transmission of Japanese asset study
subfiles.from: H. F., Adviser on International Economic Affairs
subfiles.about: Forwards principal results of a new study of Japan’s external resources.
subfiles.summary: The adviser sends a summary based on detailed Federal Reserve and Treasury material.

subfiles.title: Japanese Gold and Foreign Exchange Resources: summary
subfiles.about: Estimates Japan’s internationally realizable assets through 1938.
subfiles.summary: The memorandum estimates a decline from $789 million at the end of 1936 to $487 million at the end of 1938. It identifies gold, foreign exchange, securities, and silver holdings, then discusses how future trade deficits could alter the pace of depletion.

subfiles.title: Foreign and Domestic Commerce routing slip
subfiles.from: Bureau of Foreign and Domestic Commerce
subfiles.about: Routes commerce material to Hornbeck.
subfiles.summary: Brief routing slip accompanying commerce material.

subfiles.title: Letter to American Locomotive Company on Japanese finances
subfiles.from: Finance Division, Bureau of Foreign and Domestic Commerce
subfiles.about: Explains Japan’s deteriorating foreign-exchange position to an exporter.
subfiles.summary: The letter distinguishes Japan’s yen-bloc trade from foreign-exchange trade and describes import restrictions, declining Manchurian surpluses, and gold shipments. It discusses implications for exporters and encloses advice on securing payment.

subfiles.title: Confirmed Irrevocable Letter of Credit Advisable on Shipments to Japan
subfiles.from: Finance Division, Bureau of Foreign and Domestic Commerce
subfiles.about: Advises exporters to secure confirmed irrevocable letters of credit.
subfiles.summary: The release warns that import permits do not guarantee exchange permits or payment for shipments to Japan.

subfiles.title: Japanese Gold and Foreign Exchange Resources
subfiles.about: Begins a detailed study of Japan’s international assets.
subfiles.summary: The opening page estimates asset declines from $789 million in 1936 to $487 million in 1938; the memorandum continues beyond this section.
